fatal_errors: The proposed grain-boundary mechanism is incompatible with the target's bulk single-crystal specimens, in which grain-boundary interactions and sliding cannot govern the measured initial slip strength.

The intervention replaces temperature-dependent single-crystal compression, strain-rate jumps, TEM, and MSAD calculations with unspecified molecular-dynamics simulations and polycrystalline tensile tests.
It omits the central composition-dependent lattice-distortion/MSAD strengthening, cryogenic inertial dulling, and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier solute-pinning mechanisms.
The numerical predictions of 20% higher strength and 30% lower ductility are unsupported and do not correspond to the target observables.
explanation: The response is broadly about mechanical behavior in concentrated alloys and offers a nominally falsifiable correlation test, but it does not reconstruct the target study. Its key mediator—grain-boundary character—is absent from the target single crystals. It also uses unrelated temperatures, strain rates, loading modes, grain sizes, and a poorly defined compositional baseline. The proposed test varies dislocation density and boundary character without a clear factorial control, so even its own mechanism would be difficult to isolate. The arbitrary correlation threshold and unsupported quantitative outcomes provide little evidentiary value.
